(d) An item on the agenda may be postponed to a later meeting by majority vote of the city council.
(Ord. No. 18-02, § 1, 2-26-18)
156:
Acts of the city council which have the force and effect of law shall be enacted by ordinance. All other matters of business shall be considered in the form of a resolution. [Reference: Section 2.22 City Charter].
(Ord. No. 18-02, § 1, 2-26-18)
157:
(a) Every proposed ordinance shall be introduced in writing and in the form required for final adoption. No ordinance shall contain a subject which is not expressed in its title. The enacting clause shall be "It is hereby ordained by the governing authority of the City of Jefferson" and every ordinance shall so begin. [Reference: Section 2.22 City Charter].
(b) The title of an ordinance shall be read into the public record prior to any action on the ordinance. It shall not be necessary to read the entire ordinance proposed.
(c) Each ordinance shall be prepared with a place for the signature of the mayor and each council member, along with a place to attest signatures by the city clerk. Any council member voting for a given ordinance shall sign the ordinance. A council member who was not present when the ordinance was approved or who did not vote for the ordinance, or who recused due to personal interest or conflict of interest, shall not be required or expected to sign such an ordinance.
(Ord. No. 18-02, § 1, 2-26-18)
158:
A resolution may be passed at the time it is offered. Resolutions approved by the city council shall be effectuated by the signature of the mayor and attested to with signature of the city clerk.
(Ord. No. 18-02, § 1, 2-26-18)
159:
(a) On adoption of ordinances. Voting on the adoption of ordinances shall be by voice vote and the vote shall be recorded in the journal (minutes), but any member of the city council shall have the right to request a roll call vote and such vote shall be recorded in the journal. Except as otherwise provided in the city charter, the affirmative vote of a majority of councilmembers present at an official meeting shall be required for adoption of any ordinance, resolution, or motion. An abstention shall be counted as an affirmative vote [Reference: Section 2.21 City Charter].
(b) Mayor. The mayor shall vote only in the case of a tie or in the case where his or her vote will provide the third affirmative vote required for approval of a matter. The purpose of this paragraph is to preserve the presiding officer's necessary position of impartiality and help preserve an objective and impersonal approach.
(c) Abstention. No member of the city council shall abstain from voting on any matter properly brought before the city council for official action, except when such member of city council has a conflict of interest which is disclosed in writing prior to or at the meeting and made a part of the minutes. Any member of the city council present and eligible to vote on a matter and refusing to do so for any reason other than a properly disclosed and recorded conflict of interest shall be deemed to have acquiesced or concurred with the members of the majority who did vote on the question involved.
(Ord. No. 18-02, § 1, 2-26-18)
160:
(a) Neither the mayor nor any member of the city council shall vote upon or sign any ordinance, resolution, contract, or other matter in which he or she is personally interested. [Reference: Section 2.14(d) City Charter].
(b) The mayor and city council members shall abide by applicable state law with regard to not voting on matters of personal interest (O.C.G.A 36-30-6) and conflict of interest in zoning actions (Chapter 67A of Title 36, O.C.G.A.).
(Ord. No. 18-02, § 1, 2-26-18)
161:
(a) At every regular meeting of the city council (work session and voting session), the floor shall be open for public comments at one point during the meeting. The public comments section will last a maximum of 30 minutes, and speakers' comments will be limited to three minutes each. Individuals will be held to established time limits.
(b) All members of the public wishing to address the city council shall submit their name and the topic of their comments to the city clerk prior to the start of any meeting held by the city council.
(c) A member of the public shall not be authorized to comment on a matter for which a public hearing has been or will be held during the same meeting.
(d) Comments shall be addressed to the mayor or other presiding officer.
(e) The time limits established in this section may be waived by a majority vote of the city council.
(Ord. No. 18-02, § 1, 2-26-18)
162:
(a) Gaining the floor. Before a councilmember can make a motion or speak in debate, he or she must obtain the floor, or in other words, be recognized by the presiding officer as having the exclusive right to be heard at that time. The presiding officer must recognize, with a mere nod or a formal statement recognizing the councilmember, any councilmember who seeks the floor while entitled to it.
(b) Introduction. After being recognized by the presiding officer, any councilmember can introduce a motion when no other motion is being considered. A motion should begin with the words "I move that…" When necessary, a motion can be prefaced by a few words of explanation, which must not become a speech.
(c) Second. All motions, except for a point of order, require a second to be debated or considered. If there is no second, the presiding officer normally asks, "is there a second to the motion?" A motion that does not get seconded dies for lack of a second. To second a motion, a councilmember shall state "I second the motion" or "I second it" or, simply, "second." It is not necessary to obtain the floor to second a motion. A second merely implies that the motion should come before the council and not necessarily favoring a motion. A councilmember may second a motion "for discussion purposes only" and vote against the motion.
(d) Clarification. The presiding officer shall ensure the motion is offered in wording that is clear. If the motion is not clear to the presiding officer, it is the duty of the presiding officer to see that the motion is put into suitable form. Also, if the motion is unclear to a councilmember, he or she can ask that the motion be repeated, which the presiding officer can request the maker or the city clerk to do, or can do himself or herself. Until the chair states the question, the maker has the right to modify his motion as he or she pleases or to withdraw it entirely.
(e) Statement of question on the motion. Unless the wording of a motion is unclear or is out of order, the presiding officer will state the question (repeat the motion). When the presiding officer has stated the question, the motion is pending or "on the floor" for debate and discussion.
(f) Debate. Discussion on a motion does not take place until a second of the motion is made. Councilmembers shall address the mayor (or presiding officer), or address each other through the mayor or presiding officer. Debate must be confined to the merits of the question. If a councilmember strays from the motion being discussed, the presiding officer shall ask the councilmember to confine his or her remarks to the merits of the pending question. The councilmember making a motion shall have the right to speak first in debate, if he or she wishes, after the presiding officer has stated the question. No councilmember is entitled to the floor a second time in debate on the same motion on the same day as long as another councilmember who has not spoken on the motion desires the floor. The presiding officer cannot interrupt a person who has the floor so long as that person does not violate any of the council's rule and no disorder arises. The presiding officer cannot close debate so long as any councilmember who has not exhausted the right to debate desires the floor, except by order of the city council which requires a two-thirds vote.
(g) Amendment. A motion may be amended. Amendments to motions typically involve only the addition or deletion of words. If a motion is made and seconded to amend a motion, discussion ensues on the amendment first, then on the original motion as amended.
(h) Substitution. An alternative motion that is more than a simple addition or deletion of words may be offered as a substitute. If a motion is made and seconded to substitute a motion, discussion will continue on both motions and eventually the council will vote on the motion the councilmembers prefer.
(i) Postponement. A motion may be made to postpone a matter to a future meeting.
(j) Withdrawal. A motion may be withdrawn under the following circumstances: (1) the councilmember making the motion requests a withdrawal, and (2) the councilmember seconding the motion agrees to the withdrawal, and (3) either the council votes to accept the withdrawal, or the presiding officer asks if councilmembers objects to the motion's being withdrawn and if no one objects, the chair announces: "The motion is withdrawn."
(k) Adoption or rejection. Each motion must be disposed of (approved, disapproved, postponed, etc.). When debate appears to have ended, the presiding officer will call for a vote on the motion. This will normally be done with the question "there being no further discussion, are you ready for the question? The presiding officer may once more make clear the motion that is before the city council to decide. Then, the presiding officer will ask "those in favor of the motion, say aye. Those opposed, say no." Motions are decided by majority vote. The presiding officer announces the result of the vote. A tie vote rejects the motion. If the motion carries, it is adopted. If the council expressly decides against doing what the motion proposes, the motion is lost, or rejected.
(Ord. No. 18-02, § 1, 2-26-18)

As soon as a vacancy exists on an established board or commission of the city, the city manager shall place on next available work session agenda of the city council notice of said vacancy. Unless the procedure for appointment is otherwise prescribed by ordinance, the mayor will accept nominations for the vacant board or commission appointment. The appointment will be filled by majority vote of the city council.
(Ord. No. 18-02, § 1, 2-26-18)
165:
Effective January 1, 2026, the salary of the mayor shall be $12,000.00 per year. The salary of council members shall be $6,000.00 per year.
(Ord. No. 24-10, § 1, 12-16-24)
168:
The city manager shall be responsible for the preparation of a position classification and pay plan which shall be submitted to the city council for approval. Said plan may be amended with city council approval.
(Ord. No. 18-07, § 2, 3-26-18)
169:
Personnel policies shall be prepared and administered by the city manager as personnel director of all employees of the city (Reference: City Charter, Sec. 3.16). Said policies shall not be inconsistent with this chapter.
(Ord. No. 18-07, § 2, 3-26-18)
170:
(a) The city manager, or the manager's designee, shall make all appointments to fill authorized positions based on abilities that have been successfully demonstrated, relative levels of education, training, and experience of available applicants.
(b) The City of Jefferson will make all employment decisions (including decisions about hiring, promotion, transfer, demotion, evaluation, compensation, and termination) without regard to race, color, national origin, citizenship, sex, pregnancy, religion, age, disability, service in the uniformed services, genetic information, or any other classification protected by federal, state or local law.
(Ord. No. 18-07, § 2, 3-26-18)
171:
All employees once hired are subject to a six-month probationary period. The probationary period allows the supervisor(s) time to evaluate new employees and their working skills.
(Ord. No. 18-07, § 2, 3-26-18)
172:
(a) A promotion is defined as a move from one position classification to another that is assigned to a higher salary range. It shall be the policy of the city to seek qualified applicants for vacant positions giving first consideration to promoting from among those already employed by the city.
(b) An employee may not be promoted into a position in which they would have supervisory responsibility over a relative, unless the relative can be transferred to another position that would not be under the supervision of the relative that is being promoted.
(Ord. No. 18-07, § 2, 3-26-18)
173:
The city's regular business hours are 8:00 a.m. until 5:00 p.m. Monday through Friday, excluding holidays. However, an employee's work may necessitate a different schedule and, if so, the work schedule for each department shall be established by the department director with the advice and approval of the city manager.
Flextime is available to employees. Requests to work flextime must be made by the employee to his or her department director and approved by the city manager so as to minimize accrual of overtime.
(Ord. No. 18-07, § 2, 3-26-18)
174:

Full-time employees begin to accrue annual leave immediately upon employment but cannot take annual leave until after 30 days from their first day of employment. Annual leave shall be accrued according to the following schedule:

175:
All full-time employees shall earn sick leave beginning immediately upon employment at the rate of eight hours per month but cannot take sick leave until after 30 days beginning from the first day of employment. Accrued but unused sick leave will carry over from year to year. All accrued sick leave is forfeited upon termination of employment. Part-time employees do not receive any paid sick leave days.
(Ord. No. 18-07, § 2, 3-26-18)
176:
(a) Family Medical Leave Act. Full-time employees may be authorized to take leave as authorized and in accordance with the Family Medical Leave Act (FMLA).
(b) Bereavement leave. Full-time employees will be granted up to three days (24 hours) of paid leave, as approved by their department director, in the event of a death in their immediate family. Immediate family consists of parents, children, stepchildren, siblings, spouse, domestic partner, grandparents or any family member who lives with the employee and includes the same for the spouse's family. Arrangements for additional time off as unpaid leave of absence must be approved by the city manager. The city may request proof of death, for example: copy of death certificate, obituary, or pamphlet from viewing/funeral.
(c) Military leave. The city supports those who serve in the armed forces to protect our country. Employees who serve in the Armed Forces, the National Guard or the commissioned corps of the Public Health Service, as required by the federal Uniformed Services Employment and Reemployment Rights Act (USERRA) and state law are entitled to take a military leave of absence. Employees should notify their supervisor as soon as is practicable when military leave will be required, and must provide Jefferson with appropriate documentation of their military service. Such employees will be allowed leave of absence for ordered military duty without loss of pay for a period not exceeding a total of 18 work days in any one calendar year and not exceeding 18 work days in any one continuous period of absence. This means that if there is a difference between military pay for ordered military duty and the employee's salary, the city will pay the difference between regular compensation and the amount received as base pay from military service. If the Governor declares an emergency or an employee is called to active duty from the National Guard, that employee shall be paid for up to 30 days in one year, not to exceed 30 consecutive days. All other military leave is unpaid. However, an employee may elect to take annual leave instead of time off without pay for unpaid military leave.
(d) Time off to vote. Employees are permitted time off to vote in any municipal, county, state, or national political party primary or election for which such employee is qualified and registered to vote on the day on which such primary or election is held. If an employee's work schedule and the location of polling place will make it difficult for the employee to get to the polls before they close on the day a primary of election is held, the employee is entitled to take up to two hour(s) off work, at the beginning or end of shift, to cast a ballot. However, if the hours of work of such employee commence at least two hours after the opening of the polls or end at least two hours prior to the closing of the polls, then the time off for voting as provided for in this section shall not be available. This time will be unpaid. Employees who will need to take time off work to vote must inform their supervisor at least one day in advance. The city may specify the hours during which the employee may absent himself or herself as provided in this section.
(e) Jury/witness duty. The city will not discharge, discipline, threaten, or otherwise penalize an employee who is required to miss work to serve on a jury or attend a judicial proceeding in response to a subpoena or other court order or summons. Employees who are called to perform such jury duty service or witness service will continue to receive their regular compensation (less any amounts received from the court) during the period of time they must be absent from work for such jury duty service or witness service, for up to two weeks. The employee must notify their supervisor of their selection for jury duty or being subpoenaed, and provide a copy of the jury duty notice or subpoena. Employees are expected to make adequate arrangements for the continuation of their regular assignments while serving on a jury or as a witness. However, if employee is in court on his or her own behalf, the employee will not receive their regular compensation and instead must take annual leave, compensatory time, or a leave of absence, as approved by the employee's department director or city manager, as appropriate.
(f) Leave of absence. Employees are eligible for a leave of absence without pay for good and sufficient personal reasons, and provided that no significant disruption to the city's activities will result. Each case will be considered individually. Requests for a leave of absence must be submitted in writing to the city manager. Employees on a leave without pay are required to pay all costs for health, life insurance, accidental death and dismemberment, and retirement benefits. Employees on leave without pay will not lose any employment benefits or seniority accrued before the date on which leave commenced. An unpaid personal leave of absence, if approved, will be granted for a minimum of one week or up to 30 days. Requests for a leave of absence for other than military leave or Family and Medical Leave Act leave should be made with the full understanding that while the city will make every effort to have a comparable position with comparable pay for the employee upon return from leave, the city cannot guarantee that the employee's same position will be available upon that employee's return. Reinstatement will be dependent upon an available opening for which the employee is qualified. If the employee does not report to work at the end of the authorized personal leave of absence, that employee will be assumed to have voluntarily resigned.
(Ord. No. 18-07, § 2, 3-26-18)
177:
(a) On occasion, the city will need employees to work overtime hours. Employees are expected to work overtime as needed. Repeated refusals to work overtime when requested and/or refusal to work overtime without a valid excuse may be grounds for discipline, up to and including termination. The city will try to give employees advance notice when overtime work is necessary; however, it will not always be possible to notify workers in advance.
(b) Nonexempt employees are entitled to payment for overtime, according to the rules set forth below:
(1) All overtime work must be approved in writing, in advance, by the employee's supervisor or the city manager. Working overtime without permission violates the city's policy and may result in disciplinary action. For purposes of calculating how many hours an employee has worked in a day or week, the city's workweek begins at 12:01 a.m. on Wednesday and ends at midnight on the following Tuesday. The city's workday begins at 12:01 a.m. and ends at midnight each day.
(2) Nonexempt employees who are covered by the provision of the federal Fair Labor Standards Act will receive overtime pay at the rate of one and one-half times the employees hourly rate as follows:
a. Non-exempt, non-public safety employees and who work over 40 hours in a given workweek;
b. Non-exempt law enforcement employees who work over 86 hours in a 14-day work period;
c. Non-exempt fire protection employees who work over 212 in a specified 28-day work period.
The city is exempt from paying overtime to law enforcement or fire protection employees if the city employs less than five such employees during the workweek. Only time actually spent working counts as hours worked. Vacation time, sick days, holidays, or any other paid time during which an employee did not actually work will not count as hours worked.
(Ord. No. 18-07, § 2, 3-26-18)
178:
The city manager may lay off employees for lack of work, budgetary restrictions, reorganizations or other changes that have taken place. Dismissal action without cause may be necessary if the employee's work assignment is completed or available program funds are discontinued or cut back, or where departmental reorganization is necessary. In such case, any appeal procedure set forth in personnel policies and procedures shall not be applicable.
(Ord. No. 18-07, § 2, 3-26-18)
179:
Employment is at-will. This means employees are free to resign from their employment with the City of Jefferson at any time just as the city is free to terminate an employee at any time, for any reason, with or without notice, with or without cause, for any reason not prohibited by law.
(Ord. No. 18-07, § 2, 3-26-18)
180:
All employees, whether or not subject to division 2 of this article, shall conduct themselves in accordance with the following ethical standards of conduct. Failure to adhere to these ethical principles shall be cause for disciplinary action by the city manager in accordance with adopted personnel policies and procedures.
(a) Employees shall not accept any gifts, loans, rewards, favors, or services that may reasonably tend to improperly influence them in the discharge of their official duties. This limitation is not intended to prohibit the acceptance of articles of negligible value, which are distributed generally nor to prohibit employees from accepting loans from regular lending institutions. It is particularly important that employees guard against relationships that might be construed as or give the appearance of favoritism, coercion, unfair advantage or collusion.
(b) Employees shall not use or attempt to use their position to secure an economic benefit or advantages, special privileges or exemptions for themselves or others including the use of knowledge obtained by or through their employment or by virtue of their position.
(c) Employees shall not accept employment or engage in any business or professional activity which they may reasonably expect would require or induce them to disclose confidential information acquired by them by reason of their official position.
(d) Employees shall not accept payment from outside sources for professional services (i.e., teaching, instructing, speaking engagements, consulting, honorariums) when such activities are done on city time or when such services pertain to the purchase or sale of city property.
(Ord. No. 18-07, § 2, 3-26-18)
181:
(a) City employment shall be considered to be the primary employment of all full-time employees. No employee may engage in outside employment that will interfere with the interest of city service. Standards by which some employment is not acceptable include, but are not limited to:
(1) Illegal activity;
(2) Employment that, by virtue of association, will reflect upon the reputation of the city; or
(3) High hazard of fatiguing work, which might detract from or reduce city performance.
(b) Prior to beginning any regularly scheduled outside employment, employees will obtain specific written approval from their department head or his designee on request forms which indicate the name of the outside employer, the nature of the work, hours of work, address and telephone number where the employee can be reached. Such information will become a part of the employee's official personnel record. Employees are required to obtain approval from their department head or his designee for any change in a previously approved outside employment request.
(c) Any employee accepting or engaging in outside employment under the terms of this rule shall make arrangements with the outside employer to be available immediately to any emergency call of duty whenever the department head or his designee shall determine that the employee's services are necessary.
(d) Employees sustaining injuries while engaged in outside employment are normally ineligible to receive benefits under the city's worker's compensation program. If an employee sustains an injury while engaged in outside employment, but is performing duties, within the scope of his city responsibilities (i.e., a police arrest), he may be eligible for partial city worker's compensation benefits.
(e) Failure to comply with the provisions of this section will result in disciplinary action by the city manager in accordance with adopted personnel policies and procedures.
(Ord. No. 18-07, § 2, 3-26-18)
184:
(a) The public judges its government by the way public officials and employees conduct themselves in the posts to which they are elected or appointed.
(b) All government, of right, originates with the people, is founded upon their will only; and is instituted solely for the good of the whole. Public officers are the trustees and servants of the people and are at all times amendable to them.
(c) The people of this state have the inherent right of regulating their internal government. Government is instituted for the protection, security, and benefit of the people; and at all times they have the right to alter or reform the same whenever the public good may require it.
(d) The people have a right to expect that every public official will conduct himself in a manner that will tend to preserve public confidence in and respect for the government he represents.
(e) Such confidence and respect can best be promoted if every public official, whether paid or unpaid, and whether elected or appointed, will uniformly:
(1) Treat all citizens with courtesy, impartiality, fairness, and equality under the law; and
(2) Avoid conflicts between his private self-interest and the public interest.
(Ord. of 9-10-2001, preamble; Ord. No. 18-06, § 1, 3-26-18)
185:
The following words, terms and phrases, when used in this article, shall have the meanings ascribed to them in this section, except where the context clearly indicates a different meaning:
City official or official means the mayor, members of the city council, municipal court judges (including substitute judges), city manager, assistant city managers, city clerk, deputy city clerks, whether such person is salaried, hired or elected, and all other persons holding positions designated by the city charter, as it may be amended from time to time. The term "city official," unless otherwise expressly defined, includes individuals appointed by the mayor and city council to all city commissions, committees, boards, task forces, or other city bodies unless specifically exempted from this article.
Decision means any ordinance, resolution, contract, franchise, formal action or other matter voted on by the city council and other city board or commission, as well as the discussions or deliberations of the council, board, or commission which can or may lead to a vote or formal action by that body.
Discretionary authority means the power to exercise any judgment in a decision or action.
Entity means a sole proprietorship, partnership, limited partnership, firm, corporation, professional corporation, holding company, joint stock company, receivership, trust or any other entity recognized by law through which business may be conducted.
Immediate family means spouse, mother, father, brother, sister, son, or daughter of any city official.
Incidental interest means an interest in a person, entity or property which is not a substantial interest and which has insignificant value.
Remote interest means an interest of a person or entity, including a city official, who would be affected in the same way as the general public. The interest of a councilmember in the property tax rate, general city fees, city utility charges, or a comprehensive zoning ordinance or similar decisions is incidental to the extent that the councilmember would be in common with the general public.
Substantial interest means a known interest, either directly or through a member of the immediate family, in another person or entity:
(1) The interest is ownership of five percent or more of the voting stock, shares or equity of the entity or ownership of $5,000.00 or more of the equity or market value of the entity;
(2) Funds received by the person from the other person or entity either during the previous 12 months of or the previous calendar year equaled or exceeded $5,000.00 in salary, bonuses, commissions, or professional fees or $5,000.00 in payment for goods, products or nonprofessional services, or ten percent of the recipient's gross income during that period, whichever is less;
(3) The person serves as a corporate officer or member of the board of directors or other governing board of the for-profit entity other than a corporate entity owned or created by the city council; or
(4) The person is a creditor, debtor, or guarantor of the person or entity in an amount of $5,000.00 or more.
Substantial interest in real property means an interest in real property, which is an equitable or legal ownership with a market value of $5,000.00 or more.
(Ord. of 9-10-2001, art. III; Ord. No. 18-06, § 1, 3-26-18)
186:
(a) Any persons violating any provisions of this division is subject to:
(1) Written and oral reprimand by the adjudicating city official with jurisdiction; and
(2) A fine not less than $100.00 but no more than $500.00 to be imposed by the adjudicating city official with jurisdiction; and
(3) A request for resignation.

(a) It is the policy of the city that the proper operation of democratic government requires that public officials be independent, impartial and responsible to the people; that governmental decisions and policy be made in proper channels of the governmental structure; that public office not be used for personal gain; and that the public have confidence in the integrity of its government. (a) No city official shall use such position to secure special privileges or exemptions for such person or others, or to secure confidential information for any purpose other than official responsibilities.

(a) Who may file. There are no limitations on who may file an ethics complaint against a city official.
(b) Timing. To discourage the filing of ethics complaints solely for political purposes, complaints shall not be accepted against a person seeking election as a city official, whether currently serving as a city official or not, from the date qualifying opens for the elected office at issue through the date the election results for that office are certified. Properly filed complaints against a person seeking election as a city official will be accepted and processed after the election results have been certified.
(c) To whom a complaint is directed. All complaints against city officials other than the city manager shall be filed with the city manager. If the complaint involves the city manager, it shall be filed with the city attorney. If the complaint involves both the city manager and the city attorney, the complaint shall be filed with the judge of the Jefferson municipal court. The city manager (or city attorney or city judge if he or she has jurisdiction) may require that oral complaints, and complaints illegibly or informally drawn, be reduced to a memorandum of complaint. All complaints shall be submitted and signed under oath, shall be legibly drawn, and shall clearly address matters within the scope of this division.
(d) Notice to person charged. The city manager (or city attorney or city judge if he or she has jurisdiction) shall cause the complaint to be served on the city official charged as soon as practicable but in no event later than seven calendar days after receipt of a proper, verified complaint. Service may be by personal service, by certified mail, return receipt requested or by statutory overnight delivery.
(e) Initial review and action by city official with jurisdiction. The city manager (or city attorney or city judge if he or she has jurisdiction) shall review the complaint to determine whether the complaint is unjustified, frivolous, patently unfounded or fails to state facts sufficient to invoke disciplinary action. The city manager (or city attorney or city judge if he or she has jurisdiction) is empowered to conduct investigations, to take evidence, and to hold hearings to address the subject matter of a complaint. The city official with jurisdiction is empowered to dismiss in writing complaints that he or she determines are unjustified, frivolous, patently unfounded or fail to state facts sufficient to invoke disciplinary action; provided, however, that a rejection of such complaint by the city official with jurisdiction if applicable shall not deprive the complaining party of any action such party might otherwise have at law or in equity against the city official. For complaints that are not dismissed, the city official with jurisdiction is empowered to collect evidence and information concerning any complaint and add the findings and results of its investigations to the file containing such complaint. The city official with jurisdiction shall have no more than 60 days from the date a complaint is filed to investigate the complaint.
(f) Hearing. Unless the complaint is dismissed by the city official with jurisdiction, it shall be scheduled for hearing by the municipal court judge of the City of Jefferson, who shall hear and render decisions on all properly verified ethics complaints filed under this division. If the complaint involves the municipal judge, the complaint shall be scheduled for hearing by the Jefferson city council. Any city official charged with a violation of this division shall have a right to written notice of the hearing and the allegations at least seven calendar days before the hearing. Any city official charged with such violation is entitled to representation by legal counsel, and an adequate opportunity to respond to the charges. The hearing shall include the taking of testimony and the cross-examination of available witnesses.
(g) Disposition. The decision of the municipal court judge or city council, whichever has jurisdiction, shall be rendered within ten calendar days after completion of the hearing. Upon a finding by the municipal court judge or city council, whichever has jurisdiction, that a violation of this division by the city official complained have has occurred beyond a reasonable doubt, the judge or city council as the case may be shall determine and apply the penalty or penalties prescribed by this division. If a violation of this division is not found, the complaint shall be dismissed.
(Ord. No. 18-06, § 1, 3-26-18)

Catered event means an event at a location not otherwise licensed for consumption of alcoholic beverages by the drink at which alcoholic beverages are furnished, for consideration, and sold, dispensed or provided free of charge to persons present at the event, by the drink, pursuant to a permit obtained under this chapter.
City means the City of Jefferson, Georgia.
City clerk means the person holding the official title of clerk for the city.
City council: The Mayor and City Council of the City of Jefferson, Georgia.
Church means a body of communicants gathered into church order: united under one form of government by the profession of the same faith and the observance of the same ritual and ceremonies, place where persons regularly assemble in a facility for worship, congregation, or organization for religious purposes.
College campus means a collection of two or more buildings used for educational purposes, on either one parcel or contiguous parcels that are under the same ownership by either a public or private institution of higher learning.
Commissioner means the state revenue commissioner.
Department means the state Department of Revenue.
Distilled spirits means any alcoholic beverage obtained by distillation or containing more than 24 percent alcohol by volume.
Distillery means a facility that manufactures distilled spirits.
Eating establishment means any public place, including a place available for rent by the public, selling prepared food for consumption by the public on the premises with a full service kitchen (a full service kitchen will consist of a three-compartment pot sink, a stove or grill permanently installed, and refrigerator, all of which must be approved by the health and fire departments), prepared to serve food every hour they are open and deriving at least 50 percent of its total annual gross food and beverage sales from the sale of prepared meals or food.
Establishment means any physical location or section thereof for the operation of a business.
Food caterer means any person who holds a valid business license and for consideration, prepares food for consumption off the premises.
Fortified wine means any alcoholic beverage containing not more than 24 percent alcohol by volume made from fruits, berries, or grapes either by natural fermentation or by natural fermentation with brandy added. The term includes, but is not limited to, brandy.
Gallon or wine gallon means a United States gallon of liquid measure equivalent to the volume of 231 cubic inches or the nearest equivalent metric measurement.
Georgia farm winery means a farm winery which is licensed by the state to manufacture wine in Georgia.
Growler means a reusable, resealable, and professionally sanitized glass jug used to transport malt beverages or wine for off-premises consumption that is not to exceed 64 ounces and is filled with malt beverages or wine from a keg by a licensee, or an employee of a licensee, with a malt beverage and/or wine license for consumption on premises issued by the City of Jefferson.
Hard cider means an alcoholic beverage obtained by the fermentation of the juice of apples, containing not more than six percent alcohol by volume, including, but not limited to, flavored or carbonated cider. For purposes of this chapter, hard cider shall be deemed a malt beverage. The term does not include "sweet cider."
Hotel means any building or other structure providing sleeping accommodations for hire to the general public either transient, permanent or residential. Such hotels shall maintain a minimum of 50 rooms available for hire and have one or more public dining rooms with adequate kitchens. Motels meeting the qualifications set out herein for hotels shall be classified in the same category as hotels. Hotels shall have the privilege of granting franchises for the operation of any licensed establishment herein and the holder of such franchise shall be included in the definition of a hotel hereunder.
Importer means any person who imports an alcoholic beverage into this state from a foreign country and sells the alcoholic beverage to another importer, broker or wholesaler and who warehouses a stock of the alcoholic beverage.
Indoor commercial recreational establishment means, and is limited to, establishments:
(1) Regularly serving prepared food, with a full service kitchen (a full service kitchen will consist of a three-compartment pot sink, a stove or grill permanently installed, and a refrigerator, all of which must be approved by the health and fire departments), prepared to serve food every hour they are open and deriving at least 70 percent of its total annual gross sales from the sale of prepared meals or foods and recreation activities; and
(2) Wherein the sale of food and alcoholic beverages is incidental to its primary enterprise and activity on the premises.
The primary activity on the premises of the indoor commercial recreational establishment shall be family-oriented in nature, generally meaning a use that attracts a range of individuals from all age groups. Uses may specifically include, but are not limited to, dinner theaters, bowling centers, and other similar uses. Outdoor commercial recreation is not included, nor shall concession sales of alcoholic beverages be permitted. Bingo parlors, dancehalls, nightclubs, taverns, billiard parlors, video arcades, skating arenas, adult entertainment and/or sexually related entertainment activities and similar uses are specifically excluded from this definition of indoor commercial recreational establishments; provided that no indoor commercial recreational establishment shall offer alcoholic beverages for sale during the time it is sponsoring events that primarily attract persons under the lawful drinking age in the state.
Indoor publicly owned civic and cultural center means and is limited to publicly owned establishments wherein the sale of food and alcoholic beverages is incidental to its primary enterprise and activity on the premises. The term "indoor publicly owned civic and cultural center" may include renovated courthouses, recreational clubhouses, performing arts centers, and theaters used as civil and cultural centers.
License means an authorization granted by the city to operate as a retail consumption dealer, retail package dealer, wholesale dealer or other activity permitted and regulated by this chapter.
Licensee means any person who holds a license from the city to engage in the selling, manufacturing, distributing or importing at retail or wholesale, of any alcoholic beverages.
Liter means a metric measurement currently used by the United States.
Malt beverage means any alcoholic beverage obtained by the fermentation of any infusion or decoction of barley, malt, hops, or any other similar product, or any combination of such products in water, containing not more than 14 percent alcohol by volume and including ale, porter, brown, stout, lager beer, small beer, and strong beer. The term does not include sake, known as Japanese rice wine.
Managing agent means an individual that is at least 21 years of age, is a U.S. citizen or an alien lawfully admitted for permanent residency, is a resident of the State of Georgia, has day-to-day managerial authority over the business conducted on the licensed premises including the sale of alcoholic beverages, and is employed full-time by the licensed business.
Manufacturer means any maker, producer or bottler of an alcoholic beverage. The term also means: in the case of distilled spirits, any person engaged in distilling, rectifying, or blending any distilled spirits; provided, however, that a vintner that blends wine with distilled spirits to produce a fortified wine shall not be considered a manufacturer of distilled spirits; in the case of malt beverages, any brewer; and in the case of wine, any vintner.
Micro-brewery means a facility that produces and packages malt beverages for distribution, retail or wholesale, on or off the premises, and which has a production capacity of no more than 15,000 barrels per year. A micro-brewery that serves malt beverages for consumption on the premises is required to meet the licensing requirements of this chapter for on-premises consumption of beer and wine. A micro-brewery may also serve food but does not necessarily meet the definition of an eating establishment and is not required to provide any food service.
Minor means any person less than 21 years of age.
Multi-use facility means a structure containing three or more retail or office establishments and one or more eating establishments, which has a court area for pedestrian use.
Non-profit, charitable and civic organization means a bona fide nonprofit civic organization which is exempt from federal income tax pursuant to the provisions of subsection (c), (d), or (e) of 26 U.S.C. Section 501.
Open air cafe means a premise located within the pedestrian court area and adjacent sidewalk of a multi-use facility where food is available for purchase during all hours of operation and where alcoholic beverages may be purchased from a restaurant contained within the multi-use facility for consumption within the open air cafe.
Package means a bottle, can, keg, barrel, or other original consumer container.
Person means any individual, firm, partnership, cooperative, nonprofit membership corporation, social club, joint venture, association, company, corporation, limited liability company, limited liability partnerships, agency, syndicate, estate, trust, business trust, receiver, fiduciary or other group or combination acting as a unit, body politic or political subdivision, the plural as well as the singular member, whether public, private or quasi-public.
Premises means one physically identifiable place of business operated by the same ownership and/or overall management consisting of one or more contiguous rooms with only one address registered as a single place of business with the local licensing authority and the state. "Premises" is further defined to include: outdoor areas or patios approved pursuant to this chapter, pedestrian court areas and sidewalks in front of a building.
Private club means any nonprofit association organized under the laws of this state which: has been in existence at least one year prior to the filing of its application for a license to be issued pursuant to this chapter; has at least 75 regular dues-paying members; owns, hires or leases a building or space within a building for the reasonable use of its members, which building or space has suitable kitchen and dining room space and equipment and is staffed with a sufficient number of employees for cooking, preparing and serving meals for its members and guests; and has no member, officer, agent or employee directly or indirectly receiving, in the form of salary or other compensation, any profits from the sale of alcoholic beverages beyond a fixed salary as defined by state law.
Private function means any affair where attendance is by invitation only, where no business transactions are conducted during the private function and there is no cost to attend or to consume the food or alcohol either by donations or by any other means.
Residence means the act or fact of living or regularly staying at or in some place for the discharge of a duty or the enjoyment of a benefit or the place where one actually lives as distinguished from his domicile or place of temporary sojourn.
Resident means a person whose primary residence is within the territorial limits of the county.
Retail consumption dealer means any person who sells alcoholic beverages for consumption on the premises at retail only to consumers and not for resale.
Retail package dealer means any person who sells unbroken packages at retail only to consumers and not for resale.
School means an organized source of education or training whether public or private for the teaching of children in which the traditional subjects and learning processes associated with the Pre-K—12 grades of school are taught.
Shipper means any person who ships an alcoholic beverage from outside this state.
Tap room means an establishment that serves malt beverages (beer) and/or wine but not distilled spirits for consumption on the premises. A tap room may also serve food but does not meet the definition of an eating establishment and is not required to provide any food service. A tap room is required to meet the requirements of this chapter for the on-premises consumption of beer and wine (i.e., retail consumption dealer).
Tasting room means an outlet for the promotion of a Georgia farm winery's wine by providing samples of such wine to the public and for the sale of such wine at retail for consumption on the premises and for sale in closed packages for consumption off the premises. Samples of wine can be given free of charge or for a fee.
Wholesaler or wholesale dealer means any person who sells alcoholic beverages to other wholesale dealers, to retail dealers, or to retail consumption dealers. This shall include any person that transports or delivers alcoholic beverages from a manufacturer for sale at retail by the package.
Wine means any alcoholic beverage containing not more than 24 percent alcohol by volume made from fruits, berries, or grapes either by natural fermentation or by natural fermentation with brandy added. The term includes, but is not limited to, all sparkling wines, champagnes, combinations of such beverages, vermouths, special natural wines, rectified wines, and like products. The term does not include cooking wine mixed with salt or other ingredients so as to render it unfit for human consumption as a beverage. A liquid shall first be deemed to be a wine at that point in the manufacturing process when it conforms to the definition of wine contained in this section.
Wine tasting means an event as defined in the rules and regulations of the department of revenue.

248:
(a) Findings: It is the finding of the city council that public nudity and seminudity, under certain circumstances, particular circumstances relating to the sale and consumption of alcoholic beverages in so-called "nude bars" or establishments offering so-called "nude entertainment," "adult entertainment" or "erotic entertainment" begets criminal behavior and tends to create undesirable community conditions. Among the acts of criminal behavior identified with nudity and alcohol are disorderly conduct, prostitution, and drug trafficking and use. Among the undesirable community conditions identified with nudity and alcohol are depression of property values in the surrounding neighborhoods, increased expenditure for and allocation of law enforcement personnel to preserve law and order, increased burden on the judicial system as a consequence of the criminal behavior hereinabove described, and acceleration of community blight by the concentration of such establishments in particular areas. Therefore, the limitation of nude or seminude conduct in establishments licensed to sell alcohol for consumption on the premises is in the public welfare and is a matter of governmental interest and concern to prevent the occurrence of criminal behavior and undesirable community conditions normally associated with establishments which serve alcohol and also allow and/or encourage nudity or seminudity.
(b) No adult entertainment facility shall serve, sell, distribute or suffer the consumption or possession of any distilled spirits, wines, malt beverages, or any other alcoholic beverages or controlled substance upon its premises.
(c) Notwithstanding the prohibitions of this section, nothing in this section shall or is intended to apply to theatrical or motion picture performance houses, museums, or the like where the consumption or service of alcohol is not a primary purpose or mainstream activity of such establishment.
(Ord. No. 23-03, § 2(Att.), 10-23-23)

253:
To qualify for an alcoholic beverage license, an applicant shall meet the following:
(a) Designation of managing agent. Designate a managing agent that meets the qualifications specified in this article. In the case of a non-profit private club, the managing agent may be an officer of the non-profit private club in lieu of a full-time employee if the individual is otherwise qualified.
(b) Building and building occupancy.
(1) No alcoholic beverage license shall be issued to any person unless the building in which the business will be located is complete and detailed plans of said building and outside premises are attached to the application or unless proposed plans and specifications and a building permit of a proposed building to be built are attached to the application. The completed building shall comply with ordinances of the city, regulations for the state revenue commissioner, and the state.
(2) Each building in which the business will be located shall contain sufficient lighting so that the building itself and the premises on all sides of the building are readily visible at all times from the front of the street on which the building is located so as to reveal all of the outside premises of such building.

If the applicant is a franchisee, then such applicant shall attach a copy of the franchise agreement or contract with the application.
(4) All premises for which an alcoholic beverage license shall be issued shall afford therein adequate sanitary toilet facilities and shall be adequately illuminated so that all hallways, passageways, and open areas may be clearly seen by the customers therein.
(c) Issuance. Where the application is made on behalf of a corporation, partnership, limited liability corporation, limited liability partnership or sole proprietorship, the license shall be issued jointly to the organization and an individual that meets the qualifications of a managing agent.

255:
Unless inconsistent with the state-wide centralized application process, the following are required for the issuance of a license under the terms of this chapter. In the event that city requirements exceed those of the state-wide, centralized application process, the requirements of the city shall be met with the local application.
(a) Application. Any person desiring to obtain an alcoholic beverage license in the city shall submit a written and signed application on forms provided by the city and in connection therewith, shall, under oath, answer all questions, supply all information, and furnish all certificates, affidavits, bonds and other supporting data as required by the city. The written application for the license shall be a permanent record, and the licensee must maintain current and accurate information within said application as required by this chapter.
(b) In-person application. In addition to any online application procedure for state-wide centralized permitting, all applications for licenses to sell alcoholic beverages of any kind shall be made in person by the applicant to the city clerk or designee and shall contain but not be restricted to the following statements and information:
(1) The name, age, address and length of residency of applicant. Residency by an applicant within the city issuing the license is not a requirement because the applicant is required to designate a resident of the county who shall be responsible for any matter relating to the license.
(2) The name of the corporation, partnership, sole proprietorship, or other organization applying for the license. Said name shall include the legal name as well as the trade name of the business.
(3) A statement of whether the applicant or any person with an interest in the application has made application at any previous time for any alcoholic beverage license and the disposition of such application.
(4) Whether the applicant or any person with an interest in the application has ever been convicted of a crime, other than for traffic violations.
(5) Whether a previous license issued to the applicant or any person with interest in the application has been revoked by any state or subdivision thereof or by the federal government and the reason therefor.
(6) The identity of any other person interested directly or indirectly in the profits or losses or both of the proposed business.
(7) The physical address and detailed plans of such building and outside premises, and evidence of ownership of the building, or a document that evidences the right of the applicant to use the premises, including but not limited to a deed, lease, sublease, management agreement, or concession agreement, shall be attached to the application.
(8) Every new application for a package license hereunder shall be accompanied by a drawing to scale, showing the nearest church, school or college or by the affidavit of a registered surveyor that the proposed location of the business complies with the distance requirements as specified in this chapter. Applications for renewal of licenses, or for premises that have been licensed in the preceding 12 months, are exempted from this subsection.
(c) Fingerprinting. As provided in O.C.G.A. § 3-3-2, as a prerequisite to the issuance of any such initial permit or license only, the applicant/owner shall furnish a complete set of fingerprints to be forwarded to the Georgia Bureau of Investigation, which shall search the files of the Georgia Crime Information Center for any instance of criminal activity during the two years immediately preceding the date of the application. The Georgia Bureau of Investigation shall also submit the fingerprints to the Federal Bureau of Investigation under the rules established by the United States Department of Justice for processing and identification of records. The federal record, if any, shall be obtained and returned to the governing authority submitting the fingerprints.
(d) License fees. The license fees as required by the city are due and payable upon the filing of the application. Any person who is doing business on or after the first day of January shall pay the full annual license fee without proration; provided, however, that if an application is filed after July 1st, the license fee shall be one-half of the annual license fee for such calendar year. All new applications for alcoholic beverage licenses shall be accompanied either by lawful money of the U.S., or by a certified check, cashier's check or money order, payable to the city for the proper amount of the license fee. If the application is denied or if the applicant withdraws the application prior to its being issued, the license fee shall be refunded, less an administrative fee established by fee schedule which shall be retained by the city. The annual license fee to be charged by the city pursuant to this chapter shall be established by fee schedule and shall not be more than $5,000.00 for each license.
(e) Fee for late application. Any person holding any license issued pursuant to the Georgia Alcoholic Beverages Code and this chapter who fails to file a proper application for a similar license for the following year, with the proper fee accompanying the application, on or before the renewal date specified and who files an application after such renewal date shall be required to pay, in addition to the license taxes imposed by the Georgia Alcoholic Beverages Code and this chapter, an additional amount as specified in a fee schedule.
(f) Criminal background check. Upon receipt by the city clerk or designee of any application for an alcoholic beverage license, or for the transfer of any license, each person listed on the application shall consent to a criminal background check on the forms supplied by the city clerk or designee.
(g) Approval. All applications for alcoholic beverage licenses shall require approval by the city clerk or designee. Decisions shall be made in accordance with the standards and criteria specified in this article.
